newsitem.title: ITALY: ALPINE SKIING-ITALY ECSTATIC AT TOMBA VICTORY.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-ITALY ECSTATIC AT TOMBA VICTORY.

text.p: Italy reacted with undisguised joy on Friday to Alberto Tomba's first World Cup win of the season, adding to the burden of expectations already piled on him ahead of the world championships.

"Albertone: Yeees!", shouted the daily Gazzetta dello Sport's front page headline after the double world and triple Olympic champion won a slalom in Schladming, Austria, on Thursday and ended all doubts about his form.
"Tomba wins in the slalom and now makes us dream of the world title," it added, somewhat superfluously.
"Illuminated by Tomba," declared Tuttosport, referring to the fact that the race was under floodlights just as the slalom and giant slalom at Sestriere will be.
"Now the party can begin. Magical Tomba of the good old days, a champion who seems to have stopped time.
The championships start in Sestriere, where Tomba won his first ever World Cup race in 1987, on Monday although the Italian will not be in action until the following week.
The men's slalom on February 15 is the final event of the championships, just before the closing ceremony, and is by far the highlight race as far as Italians are concerned.
The Italian will also provide the initial media feeding frenzy with a news conference scheduled for Sunday.
The Corriere dello Sport declared the 30-year-old Bolognese the "thunderbolt" of the world championships.
"Tomba shouts: The championships are mine," it said.
Tomba has raced only a handful of races this season after being injured in training in October and then suffering a heavy bout of influenza early in January.
Tired and jaded, the Italian had considered retiring at the end of last season after two golds at the Sierra Nevada championships in Spain.
But the prospect of championships at home -- never mind the commercial incentives -- changed his mind.
Before Thursday's slalom he had finished second twice while Austrian Thomas Sykora had dominated the slalom.
Italy, and possibly Tomba himself, had resigned itself to the fact that -- while remaining Alpine skiing's superstar -- he was no longer the dominant superstar of old.
"I have had a difficult, painful, start to the season and have been slowed by so many problems," he wrote in a letter to fans in the Turin la Stampa newspaper last week.
"I will be on the piste with doubts and uncertainties...forgive me if I am unable to do what I and all of you are hoping for," he added.
After Thursday, the old, self-assured Tomba resurfaced.
The victory was the 48th of his career in the World Cup and put him alongside the great Ingemar Stenmark of Sweden, a boyhood hero, in winning a race every season for a decade.
"Until yesterday nobody believed it," the Gazzetta declared. "But everything moves along, things change.
"The Sykora of late January is not the same one as in December and, above all, Tomba is still himself."
The Italian himself declared himself ready for Sestriere.
"I am ready for a great championships, fingers crossed, but I am ready," he said in Schladming.
"This win gives me an incredible boost. There are two weeks to go before my races. Some good training, hard and concentrated, and then I will be set," he said.
The stage is set and Italy is now well and truly primed. "Incredible, magical Tomba!," declared Tuttosport.
"He's still the greatest."
